errors.code:
def sum_list(numbers):
    total = 0
    i = 1
    while i < len(numbers):
        total += numbers[i]
        i += 1
    return total
errors.why: A `while` loop that starts at index 1 silently skips the first item. No AST signal covers a while-loop start at 1 (only `range(1, ...)` is detected) and every while-based M2 example in training crashed with IndexError, so a quiet wrong sum was read as M1.

The only structural signal that fired was a `return` directly in the `while` body, and the code still passes 3 of 5 tests because the first item often decides the answer; the model split 0.50 M1 vs 0.46 M5.

close_calls.why: `try/except` swallows the IndexError that normally gives M2 away, leaving only the weak `items[n]` signal; 0.28 (M2) vs 0.27 (M5) is a coin flip that happened to land right.

close_calls.note: print with label and explicit return None
close_calls.why: An explicit `return None` defeats the structural 'prints but never returns' signal; only behavioural evidence (printed output, returned None) carried the M3 call.
